_what: The eleven guide blocks and the interim file each was copied from, at copy time. A guide block needs this because a divergence between the two copies is undetectable by construction: nothing else compares them, and this file is the only place the pairing is recorded. It is read at load, where a block whose bytes disagree with its entry is REFUSED.
_deletion: HOLD, NOT A SCHEDULE - THE TRIGGER HAS NOT FIRED. These interim files retire WITH the eleven seed blocks in this file AND with the generator's config half (render_config / cmd_apply / config_path), on the owner's ruling of 2026-10-07: ONCE EVERY SEAT HAS INSTALLED FROM A RENDER CARRYING A POLICY MODULE. The gate this note used to name - the owner ruling on the 4genthub-min room - HAS SINCE LANDED and is therefore no longer the gate; a reader who took it as the gate would delete on a condition that is already true. HOW TO CHECK THE REAL ONE, one command over the seat state dirs: the FIRST LINE of each seat's agent/AGENTS.md must be the render's marker (an HTML comment beginning 'seat-hash:') instead of the generator's header (an HTML comment beginning 'generated by scripts/seat_policy.py'). AT 2026-10-07 ALL TEN SEATS STILL CARRY THE GENERATOR'S HEADER, SO THE TRIGGER HAS NOT FIRED. AND A SECOND THING THE SAME READER MUST CHECK, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: a room whose seats pin a seat-type version that MOUNTS these blocks renders them, and it must be re-pointed before the blocks go. Today NO such room exists outside this rig - room 4genthub-dev pins seat-type 1.0.0 and a call_seat read of it returns no AGENTS.md at all (measured 2026-10-07), because the blocks ride with the 1.3.0 seat types - so this rig is the only resolver. AFTER the deletion a missing source is the steady state and the drift check reports it as source-gone rather than as a divergence. DO NOT START IT FROM THIS NOTE ALONE. AND SINCE 2026-10-08 THE FLOW ADDS A FIRST STEP TO ANY SUCH CHANGE: a change that touches structure, an interface, a boundary or the data model goes to the ARCHITECT first, which reads the code, compares at least two options, writes a short decision note and recommends one, and the lead then assigns the work with that decision attached. So the retirement is started by the lead, with the architect's decision, on the trigger - not from this note and not by a dev seat alone.
